summary: ZAR3A (زرعة, "cultivation") is a bilingual English-Arabic, mobile-friendly web app that turns NASA Earth observations into crop-rotation decisions for UAE farms. It uses NASA POWER daily and 35-year monthly climate data for Al Ain, Abu Dhabi City, and Liwa Oasis, shows NASA GIBS satellite imagery, and gives a plain-language "what to do today" action. A rotation planner compares crop sequences on water demand, heat fit, salinity fit, crop-family diversity and legume use, weighted by the farmer’s own priorities and soil salinity. It addresses the challenge by joining NASA data, local soil input, crop references (FAO-56 and the UAE planting calendar) and farmer priorities, judged against long-term climate change, not just this season. It matters because UAE farmers face heat, water scarcity, and salinity, and free NASA data is hard to use on a farm. ZAR3A makes it actionable, shows every formula, and states its limits. It is a screening tool, not a forecast.
details:
ZAR3A (زرعة) helps UAE farmers choose crop rotations using NASA Earth observations. It runs entirely in the browser, with no account, server, or API key. It calls NASA POWER directly and keeps the last good result on the device as an offline fallback.

  • Today view: daily data gives heat, rain, and humidity in plain language, plus one suggested action.
  • Climate shift: 35 years of monthly data show how temperature and rainfall have changed at each location, and provide the monthly averages used for planning.
  • Satellite view: compares high-resolution farm imagery, daily NASA true-colour imagery and the NASA vegetation index.
  • Rotation planner: for each season, it takes the planting month (UAE calendar or the farmer’s choice) and scores water demand (reference evapotranspiration × FAO crop coefficient), heat fit, salinity fit (the farmer’s soil EC against crop thresholds), crop-family diversity and legume inclusion. The farmer’s priorities weight these into a ranking. Anything that can’t be scored is left out, and every formula is shown in the app.

The interface works in English and Arabic (right-to-left) and installs as a mobile web app.

Benefit: Farmers can see which rotation uses less water or tolerates heat and salinity better, and why. Advisers get a transparent starting point for conversations.

Intended impact: Better-informed crop and planting-month choices, lower irrigation demand, more diverse rotations, and wider everyday use of NASA data by people who aren’t data specialists. It supports an agronomist’s advice and doesn’t replace it.

Tools: NASA POWER (daily and monthly), NASA GIBS (VIIRS, MODIS NDVI), Esri World Imagery, FAO-56 and FAO salinity tables, and the UAE planting calendar. Software: React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Recharts, Leaflet, Vitest.

Creativity

  • A plain-language “what to do today” action.
  • Scoring that shows its formulas and leaves out what it can’t measure, instead of guessing.
  • Honest labelling of data limits: NASA’s satellite solar series lags about 71 days, so the app says so.
  • An interactive satellite comparison.
  • An English-Arabic identity rooted in the region it serves.

Factors we considered

  • NASA values describe a grid cell, not the inside of a greenhouse.
  • It is a rule-based screening tool, not a trained model, forecast, or yield prediction, and crop coefficients are general, not calibrated to a UAE cultivar.
  • Usability: large touch targets, plain wording, and testing with agronomists and growers planned.
  • Privacy: soil inputs stay in the browser.
  • Reliability: an offline fallback and automated tests for the scoring and data parsing.
  • The Arabic translations still need native-speaker review.
